method_notes: Two-stage method. (1) 2019 baseline: Wayback Machine CDX API snapshots (2018-2019) of contradancelinks.com state schedule pages, cross-checked against Wayback snapshots of each metro's own contra-organizer site (e.g. contradance.org, thursdaycontra.com, tapestryfolkdance.org, bacds.org, sdfolkheritage.org, phxtmd.org, octds.org, hatds.org, nttds.org, dancingtheweb.com/coloradocontra, fsgw.org, cdny.org). (2) Oct-2026 current data: for 12 metros (atlanta, boston, chicago, detroit, los-angeles, minneapolis, orlando, philadelphia, phoenix, riverside, san-diego, san-francisco) read from existing per-city dossiers at folk/cities/<slug>.json (recurring_events where category=='contra_dance' and not outside_msa); for the remaining 8 metros (new-york, washington-dc, miami, tampa, dallas-fort-worth, houston, seattle, denver), current data came from fetching live organizer sites directly, since no dossier existed. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY/CAVEAT: the 2026 city dossiers were built from exhaustive multi-source research (organizer sites, Facebook, Meetup, CDSS/FAC/trycontra listings), while the 2019 baseline relies mainly on one aggregator (contradancelinks.com) plus organizer-site Wayback snapshots -- apparent "growth" in small/rural series counts for metros like Boston and Philadelphia may partly reflect better 2026 data completeness rather than real growth; flagged per-metro in notes. contradancelinks.com's own URL structure varies: most states use schedule_XX.html (2-letter code), but Massachusetts/Connecticut/Rhode Island share schedule.html, New England overview is at newengland.html, Colorado has no dedicated page (Denver data came from the secondary aggregator dancingtheweb.com/coloradocontra instead), and California is NOT split N/S (one schedule_CA.html covers the whole state). trycontra.com existed by Dec 2019 but is a dynamic zip-code tool, not retrospectively queryable via Wayback. contradancelinks.com itself stopped being meaningfully updated after ~Jan 2022 (frozen at a "as of Jan 1 2021" COVID notice), so it was used only for the 2019 baseline, never for current data. All frequencies are dances/month (weekly=4.33, 2x/month=2, monthly=1, etc.). Where 2019 evidence was partial or contradictory, confidence is marked medium/low and the gap is stated explicitly rather than guessed. Every individual metro JSON fragment below was validated with SQLite's json_valid() before assembly; the final combined object was validated with Node's JSON.parse.

detroit.notes: Flat: exactly 1/month in both 2019 and 2026, same organizer (OCTDS, founded 1991), same town (Troy), confirmed independently by two sources each era. Matches Detroit-is-at-1/month framing, with the nuance that this was ALSO true before COVID; Detroits contra scene did not decline from COVID so much as it was already thin and stayed thin. No other recurring in-metro contra series found in either year; Ann Arbor (separate MSA, excluded) is the much larger contra hub nearby.

los-angeles.notes: LAs pre-2019 organizing body was NOT SCCDC as commonly assumed; sccdc.org was a parked placeholder domain in 2018, and the real 2019 organizer was California Dance Co-operative (caldancecoop.org); SCCDC/California Twirl branding postdates 2019 (California Twirl specifically dates to 2025). series.name: PHXTMD contra (multiple rotating dates through 2019: 1st/2nd Fri, 1st/2nd Sat through mid-year, then 4th Fri + occasional 1st Sat from Aug 2019)

phoenix.notes: Phoenixs 2nd Saturday series was explicitly marked DISCONTINUED on phxtmd.org by August 2019, i.e. it already died BEFORE COVID, yet by 2026 a 2nd Saturday series is back, rotating between Chandler and Phoenix venues. Not a single clean COVID decline: pre-COVID contraction (2019), then COVID-era disruption, then apparent revival of both weekend slots by 2026, landing close to but slightly below the 2019 average. One 2019 PHXTMD listing explicitly named a DJ Flourish fusion-contra event, showing DJ/recorded-music contra already existed occasionally pre-COVID.

riverside.notes: No recurring contra series found in Riverside or San Bernardino counties in EITHER 2019 or 2026. 2019: a single one-off dance (Redlands, Jan 25 2019, University of Redlands, source https://web.archive.org/web/20190124080544/http://www.contradancelinks.com/schedule_CA.html) was found with zero other dated instances across a full year of Wayback coverage; a Riverside 1st Sunday venue description existed but zero actual scheduled dates ever appeared for it. 2026: existing dossier independently confirms zero contra series in the Inland Empire, noting residents drive west to Claremont/South Pasadena (LA County) for contra. The one metro of 20 that is a contra desert in BOTH eras, a true non-recovery because there was nothing to recover, distinct from Miami/Dallas/Denver/San Diego which had real series that shrank.

miami.notes: Sharpest, cleanest contraction found in the whole 20-metro study along with Dallas: from 3 loosely-coordinated series (~3.5/month) across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties in 2019 down to just ONE confirmed surviving series (Boca Raton, ~1/month) in 2026, roughly a 70% volume decline and consolidation from 3 counties worth of activity to effectively Palm Beach County only. seattle.notes: The single clearest full-recovery-no-net-change story in the whole 20-metro study, alongside Houston: both flagship weekly series (Lake City Thursdays, Emerald City Fridays) unchanged in frequency 2019 to 2026. Seattles gender-neutral calling transition PRE-DATES COVID entirely and is unusually well-documented: Lake City ran monthly Larks & Ravens trial dances starting in 2018 and had fully flipped over to exclusively gender-neutral calling by late 2019 (confirmed via a 2025 KNKX public-radio retrospective quoting caller Sherry Nevins directly), terminology since refined to Larks & Robins. COVID-era practices lingered unusually long: Emerald City only ended contact-tracing due to declining reports of COVID within the dance community on October 30 2026, essentially the week of this research. Tacoma shifted Saturday evening to Sunday afternoon but kept the same monthly cadence.

denver.notes: A clear ~50% contraction (4/month to 2/month), compounded by venue consolidation (two Denver venues merged into one, Wheat Ridge Grange) AND a geographic loss: the experienced-dancer Zesty dance relocated entirely into Boulder County, explicitly EXCLUDED from the Denver MSA per the task county list, so it now counts as zero for Denver even though the series itself survives. Gender-neutral (Larks and Ravens -> Larks and Robins) calling was already used at the Hands Across series specifically in 2019, but is now used uniformly across both remaining series by 2026, a within-metro spread from one specialty series to the whole scene, not a COVID-caused invention. The Westminster (Adams Co.) series had already ended September 2018, before this baseline window, showing Denvers contra scene was contracting pre-COVID too.
